issue: #407 (CRUX audit E05) — the MCP/HTTP/verb-call drift verb hashed the controller's filesystem for remote machines and dropped the census

quorum.kill_rule: any un-countered substantive objection kills the claim
refuted_claims: The unit suite in mcp::tests_drift_e05 is the falsifier for this change — REFUTED: it proves the handler, not the process an agent talks to; the three cases were rewritten through `forjar verb call drift --json` and both load-bearing mutations turn them RED.

The verb should run the config's completion_check against the target the way the CLI does, because a report that skips task checks is incomplete — REFUTED: under readOnlyHint: true an untrusted checkout would execute shell on the controller; completeness for the verb is a census entry and a named skip.

A machine with no lock hides the completion_check it would have declined — REFUTED: machine_lock pushes the machine to `unchecked` before continuing, and an unlocked machine has no converged resource whose check could be declined.
quorum.divergence: the probe lane confirmed the fix through the binary; the agy lane REJECTED it on five charges — three were correct and are taken (container/pepita at a local addr read the controller; service-task completion_checks still ran; an unknown machine answered clean), one tightened the falsifier (the MISSING verdict must show the failed reach), one was refuted (unlocked machines are disclosed as unchecked).

systems: Ansible — check mode is a contract; modules that cannot honour it skip and REPORT the skip, never execute the play's own commands
Terraform — plan refreshes by querying providers against the TARGET but never runs local-exec provisioners
Salt — test=True returns what would change and names states it could not evaluate
Puppet — --noop reports every resource it did not apply
crux.verdict: every surveyed tool queries the target under a read-only mode and none executes user-declared shell there; the verb was below that bar on both counts and is now at it.

agy_teamwork.verdict: REJECTED the first cut on five charges: local-addr containers still read the controller, service-mode tasks executed their completion_check under the read-only verb, an unknown -m answered clean, the MISSING assertion could pass vacuously, and unlocked machines hid a declined check. Four were correct and are taken; the last was refuted (unlocked machines are disclosed as unchecked).
unique_findings: a container or pepita machine at 127.0.0.1 fell through the local-addr shortcut to the controller's filesystem — taken: reads_the_controller is local-transport only
service-mode tasks bypassed task_check's decline and ran their completion_check via the generic state query — taken: declined under the same census reason

evidence.redaction: no machine-local identity in this set
known_limits: The CLI `forjar drift` still runs config-declared completion_checks by default; that is deliberate (the operator owns the config) and unchanged here.
Proves the verb contacts the declared target and declines the config's shell; does not prove every detector honours a machine argument — file, package and task are exercised.

`is_local_addr` is a string match on the address; a port-forwarded VM at 127.0.0.1 with the plain SSH transport is still read as the controller. Pre-existing; a transport-aware locality check is a separate change.
